original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Do the two predecessor E7 reflection-orbit hashes partition the weight-at-most-12 words recovered by an independent half-split of the pinned kernel?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a new measured speedup. PR #5729 already published the bit-lane speedup, and research/e7-bitslice-coverage-check compared the iterator with a full-kernel census while leaving the reflection orbits unreplayed. This package applies those frozen permutations to that recovered set and compares both receipt hashes. It does not time the engine or add another optimization.
bottleneck_link: A faster E7 exhaustion is coverage for deletion and decoder checks only when its minimum-weight words are still the classified orbits. Matching the two receipt hashes on an independently recovered set closes that gap in the published replay. It does not change a supplier bill or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the two receipt orbits are hashed with the frozen reflections and compared with one independent weight-12 census. Do not remeasure the #5729 timing claim, recompute quadratic ranks, or bind another decoder.
evidence: Two half-splits and engine batches 16 and 8 agree on zero plus 1638 weight-12 words. The frozen 63 reflections send the two receipt representatives to orbits of sizes 630 and 1008 whose SHA256 values are the receipt hashes. Those orbits are disjoint and their union is the census. Deleting one word, overlapping the orbits, or moving the diagonal representative fails.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Do the two receipt representatives still have quadratic ranks 6 and 2, with every single omission of rank 11, on this same support set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The orbit hashes identify the sets. They do not rerun the rational-lift or quadratic-form half of the classification, so the receipt is not a fully replayed theorem.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate form_a and form_b from source/verify.py on the pinned roots and compare supported_rank and quadratic_matrix with the receipt.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not recompute those ranks.

open_questions.question: Does the same orbit partition hold for one other deletion or decoder code named by the bit-lane proof?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The published iterator open question asks to bind another consumer before treating the speedup as coverage outside this E7 kernel.
open_questions.first_step: Name that code's generators, width and weight bound, then compare one half-split with low_weight_words on that basis alone.
open_questions.blocked_by: No second consumer is pinned here.
